Review the current ESP32-S31 openvela developer-platform delivery layout while Root handles board Ethernet testing. Work entirely offline. Do not access serial, USBIP, Windows network, boards, or flash. Do not build, edit maintained sources, change any Git worktree, or publish. Your only writes are reports under /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/platform-layout-review-e406.
Compare canonical board layering in openvela-dev/nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit and openvela-dev/nuttx/boards/risc-v/esp32s31/esp32s31-core-function-board, their architecture drivers and apps, against the current contest2026_497_nitelabu submission tree. The deliverable should be an engineer-facing platform with reproducible build/flash entrypoints, board support, reusable drivers and demo applications; xTS is supporting validation.
Relevant already qualified source data: /home/regex/work/esp32s31-contest-candidate-e403-v2 (36 changed projects), /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/korvo-factory-product-e403 (source export and independently verified receiver build), backups/function-ethernet-basic/files (Ethernet overlays, still under Root board validation), and backups/factory-demo-port/digit-delivery-worker (separate stable digit demo). Do not assume independently rebuilt firmware has board acceptance. Avoid recursing build trees, snapshots, Git objects or large archives; inspect top-level inventories and named manifests.
Produce concise layout-review.md plus proposed-delivery-tree.json and actionable-integration.json. Identify specific existing files to retain, obsolete generated diagnostic/evidence trees that belong in private archives, and missing build/flash entrypoints. Keep canonical upstream source paths intact; respect required contest top-level board/logs structure. Do not modify or inspect AI conversation logs; Root owns their policy and export. No changes yet: this is preparation for the integration after Ethernet validation. Report exact facts and uncertainties, with local paths.

I’ll inventory the canonical board layers and the current submission using only local files, then write the three requested review artifacts under the delivery workspace. I’ll avoid builds, maintained-source edits, Git changes, board/serial/network access, and any conversation-log inspection.

The canonical BSP and driver paths are present. The main layout issue is the submission layer: it combines snapshot/replay tooling and extensive validation material, while the newer factory export and stable digit demo live separately. I’m tracing the existing manifests and entrypoints to distinguish reusable delivery components from historical diagnostics.

The submission is materially behind the qualified source candidate: its snapshot covers 14 changed projects, versus 36 in E403-v2. Its board copy has 116 profiles versus 170 in the maintained BSP, and lacks factory, audio, touch and other newer support files. The factory receiver build is separately documented as successful, but its new firmware remains explicitly untested on hardware; I’ll preserve that distinction in the integration plan.

Two integration gaps are concrete: the old submission build wrapper omits the newer locked IDF/SDK layout, and the existing deployment helper only accepts an older SMP/AppFS profile, so it cannot serve the factory image unchanged. I also found two Ethernet overlay files whose hashes differ from their current manifest; that is consistent with ongoing work and means integration must use Root’s final frozen set. I’m now writing the proposed tree and ordered integration actions.

The three artifacts are written. They identify retained source files, private-archive candidates, profile-specific build/flash gaps, and eight ordered integration actions. I’m checking the JSON, path references and reported counts before handing them back; no integration has been performed.

Completed offline. Only the three reports were written:

- [Layout review](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/platform-layout-review-e406/layout-review.md)
- [Proposed delivery tree](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/platform-layout-review-e406/proposed-delivery-tree.json)
- [Actionable integration plan](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/platform-layout-review-e406/actionable-integration.json)

Findings: stale board mirror, 14 versus 36 changed-project coverage, and incomplete current build/flash entrypoints. Reports identify retained files and private-archive candidates.

JSON and path checks passed. Ethernet awaits Root’s final freeze; independently rebuilt firmware remains distinct from board-accepted firmware.
